detailed_rationale:
[DATA] Maruti's domestic demand cycle has genuinely turned since the GST 2.0 rate cut took effect 22-Sep-2025, which moved small cars (sub-4m, <=1200cc petrol/CNG) from the 29-31% slab to 18% and cut ex-showroom prices by as much as Rs 1.3 lakh on the Alto K10/S-Presso, with Swift/Baleno/WagonR/Fronx down 9-13%. Maruti itself has called this a demand 'reignition' for the entry-level segment it over-indexes on, and the pipeline shows it: as of the rate-cut window the company was sitting on ~3.5 lakh pending bookings, of which ~2.5 lakh were for Baleno/Swift-class cars. That tailwind is now visible in the print -- Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) total sales of 6,82,724 units were up 29.3% YoY, and June 2026 alone saw domestic PV dispatches +23.8% YoY and total sales of 2,00,390 units (+19.3% YoY) despite a scheduled one-week block shutdown for maintenance. Exports are the second, less GST-dependent engine: FY26 shipments hit a record 4.47 lakh units (+~34% YoY) across ~100 countries (Africa/Latin America/SE Asia the largest by volume), and FY26 production of 23.4 lakh units made the combined Gurugram-Manesar-Kharkhoda-Hansalpur complex the only Suzuki manufacturing footprint globally at that scale. Kharkhoda's second line began commercial production 18-May-2026, taking that site alone to 5 lakh units/year and total installed capacity to 26.5 lakh units/year -- a real supply-side unlock, since capacity (not demand) was the binding constraint through much of FY25-26. On the EV side, the e-Vitara launched 17-Feb-2026 (delayed from the original Dec-2025 date) at a BaaS starting price of Rs 10.99 lakh, with deliveries constrained until July-2026 and a 6-8 week waiting period on regular trims -- early-stage and not yet a P&L mover, but a genuine first EV entry rather than a paper launch.

[DATA]+[INFERENCE] Set against that volume recovery is a real, multi-quarter margin-compression story that our own PIT quarterly data corroborates independently of any single web source. Pulling the last ~8 quarters from our point-in-time quarterly dataset (symbol=MARUTI): PBT margin has stepped down from ~13.5-13.7% in FY24-early-FY25 (Q4FY24 13.3%, Q2FY25 13.7%) to 9.4% in Q4FY26 (PBT Rs4,918cr / sales Rs52,462cr) -- a sustained, not one-quarter, compression. FY26 full-year net profit grew only +1.2% YoY (~Rs14,680cr vs ~Rs14,500cr) despite revenue growing ~20%, and net margin compressed from 9.48% to 8.01% -- exactly the volume-growing-but-earnings-not-following pattern our charter treats as a warning sign, just running through the cost side (commodities, employee cost) rather than price-led topline inflation. Cost of materials consumed grew 27.9% YoY in FY26 versus 19.9% revenue growth, and employee costs rose 28.8% YoY. The single largest driver of the reported Q4FY26 net-profit miss (-6.5% YoY to Rs3,659cr despite record revenue) was non-operating: other income fell to Rs500cr from Rs1,528cr YoY, which the company attributed to a notional mark-to-market loss on its bond/treasury portfolio from yield movements, described as recoverable later. Cross-checking against the operating-profit line in our own PIT data, core operating profit (op_profit, i.e. PBIDT) actually grew ~27% YoY in Q4FY26, essentially in line with the 28.2% revenue growth -- so the operating engine kept pace; the headline profit miss is mostly a treasury-income and tax-rate (26% vs 20% YoY) effect layered on top of genuine but modest operating deleverage. This treasury-income dependency is itself a structural earnings-quality wrinkle worth flagging on an ongoing basis: other income has historically run 20-40% of quarterly PBT for Maruti given its large net-cash balance sheet (D/E 0.0, interest coverage 89.8x per the quant snapshot), so a debt-free balance sheet's income statement is, ironically, part-hostage to bond-yield marks. Separately, Maruti's royalty payment structure to Suzuki Motor Corporation (historically ~5-6% of net sales, once documented at ~36% of pre-royalty PBT in FY15 and termed 'extortive' by IiAS) is a standing, structural cap on margin upside for minority shareholders -- not new, but a real reason margins may not fully mean-revert even if commodity costs ease.

[DATA]+[OPINION] Competitively, Maruti's PV market share fell to 39.26% (some trackers show 38.93%) in FY26 -- a 13-year low and the third consecutive year of decline, down roughly 12 percentage points since FY20 -- almost entirely a function of SUV under-representation: utility vehicles are now ~67% of the Indian PV market, and Maruti's own UV share sits below 25% even as Tata+M&M's combined share rose to ~27% in FY26 from ~18% in FY22. The silver lining is the most recent quarter: Maruti's UV franchise (Brezza/Ertiga/Fronx/Grand Vitara/Invicto/Jimny/Victoris/e-Vitara/XL6) grew UV volumes 28.7% YoY in June 2026 to 61,726 units, a pace roughly matching M&M's own 28% UV growth that same month -- the first read in a while where Maruti's newer UV portfolio (Victoris, e-Vitara) looks like it is competing on growth rate rather than continuing to bleed share, though one month is not a trend reversal. On valuation, at the quant snapshot's ~29.5x trailing consolidated P/E (mcap Rs4,33,357cr, share price ~Rs14,366 as of 3-Jul-2026, reconciling to an EPS of ~Rs485-490 against FY26 net profit of ~Rs14,680cr / ~30.17cr shares) against a 3-year revenue CAGR of 16.0% and 1-year revenue growth of 19.9%, but net-profit growth of only +1.2% in the same FY26 -- the market is pricing continued double-digit volume growth (which the GST tailwind, export ramp and freed-up Kharkhoda capacity make reasonably likely) plus an implicit bet that the margin compression of the last two years partially reverses. Analyst target ranges cluster Rs13,200 (ICICI Securities) to Rs14,500 (Goldman Sachs) around the current price, i.e. broadly fairly-valued rather than cheap or stretched, consistent with the quant model's own Hold/Hold verdict on both horizons.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, not Sell. The volume/demand-cycle thesis is intact and, if anything, improving: GST 2.0 has genuinely reignited small-car demand (Maruti's core segment), Q1 FY27 total sales are up 29.3% YoY, exports hit a record 4.47 lakh units in FY26, and the Kharkhoda capacity unlock (26.5 lakh units/year total installed capacity) removes what had been a real supply constraint. Balance-sheet quality is clean and unambiguous (D/E 0.0, interest coverage 89.8x, bs_flag GREEN, zero red flags) -- there is no solvency or governance trigger here. But this is also not a name where the fundamental story is improving fast enough, relative to its ~29.5x multiple, to add conviction: PBT margin has compressed from ~13.5-14% to 9.4% over roughly two years on our own PIT data, FY26 net profit grew only 1.2% against ~20% revenue growth, the PV market-share erosion (13-year low, 39.26%, three straight years of decline) reflects a real and only partially-fixed SUV under-representation problem, and the royalty structure to Suzuki is a standing structural drag on margin upside that predates and will outlast this review. None of that is a thesis break -- operating profit (ex the one-off treasury/bond MTM hit) kept pace with revenue in the latest quarter, and June's UV growth (+28.7% YoY) is the first sign the newer SUV portfolio (Victoris, e-Vitara) may be competing rather than continuing to lose ground -- but it is enough to keep this at Hold rather than treat the volume recovery as a re-rating catalyst. The quant model's own Hold/Hold across 3y and 1y horizons, with mid-pack quality (45.2 pctile) and reasonable value (68.8 pctile) scores, is the right calibration: hold the existing position through the GST-tailwind volume cycle and the pending Q1 FY27 print (board meeting 31-Jul-2026), but this is not, on current evidence, a name to add fresh capital to at the current multiple given the unresolved margin-compression question.

Set against that: our own PIT quarterly data shows PBT margin compressing from ~13.5-14% (FY24/early-FY25) to 9.4% (Q4FY26), FY26 net profit grew only +1.2% YoY versus ~20% revenue growth, and PV market share fell to a 13-year low of 39.26% (three consecutive years of decline) on SUV under-representation, though June's UV growth (+28.7% YoY) is an early sign of stabilization. At ~29.5x trailing P/E the stock looks fairly valued rather than cheap or stretched -- consistent with the quant model's own Hold/Hold verdict -- pricing continued volume growth without requiring the margin story to fully repair. Call: Hold.
positive_para: GST 2.0 (effective 22-Sep-2025) has genuinely reignited demand in Maruti's core small-car segment (29-31% GST slab cut to 18%), with pending bookings of ~3.5 lakh units (~2.5 lakh for Baleno/Swift-class cars) as of the rate-cut window and Q1 FY27 total sales up 29.3% YoY to 6,82,724 units. Exports are a genuinely scaling second engine, independent of the domestic cycle: FY26 shipments hit a record 4.47 lakh units (+~34% YoY) across ~100 countries, with Africa/Latin America/SE Asia the largest markets, making Maruti's Indian complex the sole Suzuki manufacturing footprint globally producing at the FY26 record of 23.4 lakh units. Capacity, previously a binding constraint, has been unlocked -- Kharkhoda's second line began commercial production 18-May-2026, taking total installed capacity across all four plants to 26.5 lakh units/year. June 2026's UV growth of +28.7% YoY (61,726 units) is the first recent signal that Maruti's newer SUV portfolio (Victoris, e-Vitara alongside Brezza/Grand Vitara/Fronx) may be competing on growth rate with M&M/Tata rather than continuing multi-year share erosion, and the e-Vitara (launched 17-Feb-2026, BaaS pricing from Rs 10.99 lakh, 6-8 week waiting period) is a genuine, demand-constrained first EV entry. The balance sheet is unambiguously clean: D/E 0.0, interest coverage 89.8x, bs_flag GREEN, zero red flags, giving full flexibility to fund the EV/capacity capex cycle without leverage risk.

Maruti's royalty payments to Suzuki Motor Corporation (historically ~5-6% of net sales, documented at ~36% of pre-royalty PBT as far back as FY15 and termed 'extortive' by governance advisory IiAS) are a standing structural drag on margin upside for minority shareholders that predates this review and is unlikely to reverse. Competitively, PV market share fell to a 13-year low of 39.26% in FY26 (third consecutive year of decline, down ~12pp since FY20), driven by structural SUV under-representation (UVs are ~67% of the PV market; Maruti's own UV share is below 25%) while Tata+M&M's combined share rose to ~27% in FY26 from ~18% in FY22 -- June's UV growth improvement is one data point, not yet a confirmed reversal. Dealer-level discounting in July 2026 (up to Rs 90,000 on Victoris Hybrid trims, Rs 55-80k on Brezza/Victoris CNG) suggests at least some inventory-clearing pressure ahead of the festive season, though this could equally reflect normal pre-festive positioning rather than demand softness.
reverse_dcf_judgment: [OPINION] At ~29.5x trailing consolidated P/E (mcap Rs4,33,357cr against FY26 net profit of ~Rs14,680cr), the market is pricing meaningfully more than the FY26 outturn (net profit +1.2% YoY) would justify on its own -- it is effectively underwriting (a) continued double-digit volume growth, which the GST 2.0 tailwind, record export ramp and newly-unlocked Kharkhoda capacity make reasonably credible for FY27-28, and (b) at least partial reversal of the margin compression seen over the last two years (PBT margin ~13.5-14% down to 9.4%), which is far less certain given commodity-cost inflation, a GST-driven mix shift toward lower-ASP small cars, and the structurally fixed royalty drag to Suzuki. A rough sense-check: if revenue keeps compounding at the recent mid-teens-to-20%+ pace (aided by a soft FY26 base and the GST unlock) but PBT margin stays pinned near the Q4FY26 level rather than reverting toward FY24-25 levels, EPS growth lands closer to high-single-digit/low-double-digit than the mid-to-high-teens a 29-30x multiple typically wants to see from a mature, ~14% ROE auto OEM. Against that, ROCE of 20% (versus ROE of 13.7%, the gap consistent with the large net-cash balance sheet) and a debt-free structure mean the multiple is not obviously unsupportable, and the analyst target cluster (Rs13,200-14,500) sitting close to the current ~Rs14,366 price suggests the Street already treats this as fair-value-ish rather than mispriced in either direction. Net: the multiple is clearable if the volume recovery holds AND commodity/mix pressure eases even partially -- a plausible but not high-conviction base case -- which argues for holding through the cycle rather than either adding aggressively or exiting a structurally clean balance sheet on a valuation call alone. This is a directional judgment, not a formal multi-year FCF/WACC build.
escalation_reason: [INFERENCE] Genuine Hold-vs-Sell judgment tension, not a data-staleness issue: our own internal PIT quarterly data shows Maruti's PBT margin compressing from ~13.5-14% (FY24/early-FY25) to 9.4% (Q4FY26) over roughly two years, with FY26 net profit growing only +1.2% YoY despite ~20% revenue growth -- i.e., the 'volume recovery' story that supports Hold is running alongside a genuinely deteriorating earnings-conversion trend (commodity cost inflation, GST-driven mix dilution toward lower-ASP small cars, and the structurally fixed Suzuki royalty drag). At the current ~29.5x multiple, this is a real bet that margins stabilize or partially recover, not a bet the market is already discounting a further leg down. The pending Q1 FY27 results (board meeting 31-Jul-2026, a known calendarable catalyst) and the analyst-preview expectation of EBITDA margin declining further to 9.8% from 10.4% YoY are the near-term test: if margins fail to stabilize in that print, the Hold call here should be revisited toward Sell. Flagging this now rather than waiting for the print, since it is exactly the kind of 'growth headline masking earnings quality' pattern our charter treats as a warning sign, just running through costs rather than price -- worth the Principal's/CIO's own read given this is an existing, sizeable holding (holding_value_inr=133,140 in the snapshot) rather than a fresh entry decision.
